name: Salonga National Park
blurb: Bonobos, forest elephants and swamp forest in Africa's largest tropical forest reserve.

tip.title: Remove the bonobos
tip.text: Bonobos carry the seeds of many trees. Set Bonobo to -100% and watch leopards lose a prey species and insects and fruit trees shift.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Salonga National Park, Bonobo, African forest elephant). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Light reaching the canopy drives the forest; little of it reaches the shaded floor, where herbs and seedlings compete for gaps.
Year-round rain feeds the rivers and keeps the forest wet; it is the water supply for every plant here.
Rivers such as the Salonga, Lokoro and Lula spill into swamp and flooded forest, creating wetland habitat for sedges, palms and fish.
Fallen leaves, fruit and dead animals are broken down here, and the nutrients are taken up again by roots.
Break down dead plants and animals in the warm, wet forest floor and return nutrients to the soil.
Fig trees produce fruit that feeds birds, monkeys, apes and elephants, which then carry the seeds away.
Broad-leaved herbs of the forest floor and clearings, grazed by forest elephants. Marantochloa congensis is recorded near the park.
Eats bark, leaves and many kinds of fruit, and spreads large seeds far from the parent tree. Hunting is the main threat in Salonga.
Eats mostly fruit, plus leaves, invertebrates and some small animals. It is the second-largest fruit eater in the Congo forest and a major seed disperser.
About 90% fruit, with figs and oil palm fruit as staples, plus some insects. It spreads the seeds of many trees.

nodes.name: Forest insects and snails
nodes.desc: Beetles, termites, ants and other small animals of the leaf litter. They feed on plants and decaying matter and are eaten by many birds, fish and reptiles.
Takes monkeys and duikers. Leopards are among the few predators of bonobos and sitatunga.
Rainforest eagle that hunts mostly monkeys, including mangabeys, and also takes hornbills and monitor lizards.

story: Salonga National Park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is Africa's largest tropical rainforest reserve, at about 36,000 km². It has no roads, and most of it is reachable only by river. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1984.
matters: Poaching and housing construction put it on the endangered list in 1999. It was removed in 2021 after its condition improved.
